metadata.title: Hosted Stays Marketplace Residuality Stress Test
metadata.description: Explore how a hosted-stays marketplace would need to change when city permission changes, a region becomes unsafe, ownership and hosting roles split, or active stays must be relocated at short notice.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: A host verifies an account, publishes a home with one calendar and price, and accepts a booking from a guest. The marketplace assumes that the listing remains legal and usable, that the host is the owner and operator, and that the booked property will fulfill the stay.
metadata.residualArchitecture: Instead of binding the listing, property, legal permission, operating host, owner, payout recipient, booking, and physical stay into one record, the adapted design manages them separately over time. Eligibility can change without erasing a listing, roles and money can be assigned explicitly, and a guest commitment can move to a safe replacement or refund path when the original property can no longer fulfill it.
metadata.note: These tests begin with city policy, physical safety, supply organization, and active-stay obligations. An integrated change means included in the adapted model, not a claim about a particular marketplace's production implementation.

source.title: Residues: Time, Change, and Uncertainty in Software Architecture
source.author: Barry M. O'Reilly

stressors.name: A city changes short-term-rental permission street by street with 48 hours' notice
stressors.detection: City registers, permit feeds, legal notices, address and zone changes, host documents, enforcement reports, and booking-date conflicts.
stressors.attractor: A listing may remain a real and well-reviewed home while becoming ineligible for some dates, stay lengths, guest types, or host arrangements. Existing bookings and payouts outlive the permission that originally allowed them, and a single active or inactive flag cannot represent the business obligation.
stressors.businessReaction: Stop new ineligible bookings, preserve valid history, identify affected future stays, ask for new evidence where possible, offer compliant alternatives or refunds, and prove to the city which rule and permit governed every decision.
stressors.residue: Separate property, listing, address, owner, operator, permit, zone rule, booking eligibility, stay date, and marketplace decision. Effective-dated policy evaluates each proposed or existing stay; a listing remains visible to its owner with an explained restricted state, while remediation follows the exact bookings and obligations affected.

impacts.effect: Professional operators can manage compliance as a changing portfolio state instead of discovering restrictions through cancellations.
Compliance control covers permit evidence, effective dates, booking exposure, and remediation across the portfolio.
Shows which properties, dates, listings, and booked stays are affected by a specific local rule.
Active listing quality includes current legal eligibility and future booking coverage, not only content and demand quality.
Adds portfolio eligibility, permit renewal, exposure, and remediation views for professional operators.
Makes changing local eligibility part of normal portfolio operations rather than an external exception queue.
Versions local rules and evaluates them against property, operator, permit, dates, and stay terms.
Keeps listing content and history separate from whether a particular stay may currently be sold.
Blocks only the dates and stay shapes that the effective permission makes ineligible.
Owns the reusable eligibility decision and evidence standard with local operations teams.
Makes precise local compliance and low-disruption remediation a marketplace supply benchmark.

stressors.name: Wildfire makes an entire destination unsafe during active stays
stressors.detection: Civil-protection alerts, evacuation zones, air-quality and road feeds, host and guest reports, emergency-service guidance, and location-aware trip status.
stressors.attractor: Many functioning properties become unsafe at once, guests and hosts may be unreachable, ordinary cancellation rules are unfair, replacement supply changes by the hour, and the marketplace must protect people before deciding final financial responsibility.
stressors.businessReaction: Declare an affected operating area, warn and account for guests and hosts, stop unsafe arrivals, help people relocate, reserve scarce safe supply, provide emergency payment or refund paths, and reconcile responsibility after immediate safety is restored.
stressors.residue: Represent a destination operating state separately from each listing and booking. A versioned emergency policy carries geography, time, severity, affected trip phases, communication, safety actions, relocation eligibility, payment treatment, and evidence; guest commitment stays separate from the replaceable property that fulfills it.

impacts.effect: Guest trust includes coordinated safety and recovery when a whole destination, not one host, fails the stay.
Guests can recover the trip through one accountable path even when the host and original home cannot respond.
Recovery starts from the shared emergency state and offers safe relocation, refund, or assistance with visible responsibility.
Issue recovery measures safe outcomes and time to a credible plan, not only whether support contact was avoided.
Adds destination alerts, safety confirmation, relocation choices, and emergency payment status to the trip experience.
Coordinates one area-level response across guests, hosts, listings, payments, and support.
Carries current safety state, acknowledgements, help requests, and the replacement itinerary.
Opens one recovery case for relocation, assistance, refund, evidence, and later reconciliation.
Supports emergency assistance, protected funds, relocation charges, and delayed responsibility decisions.
Owns the emergency operating mode with booking, payments, policy, and local-response teams.
Makes destination-scale recovery and cross-inventory relocation a visible traveler-trust comparison.

stressors.name: Cities require every remote owner to appoint a locally licensed operating host
stressors.detection: New licensing rules, host onboarding questions, ownership documents, co-host invitations, payout instructions, local contact requirements, and enforcement notices.
stressors.attractor: The person who owns the property, controls the listing, performs local operations, communicates with the guest, carries the permit, receives revenue, and pays taxes can no longer be assumed to be one account. Informal password sharing and payout workarounds become both unsafe and illegal.
stressors.businessReaction: Let owners appoint qualified operators, verify each legal and operational role, grant only needed permissions, assign duties and money explicitly, show guests the accountable local host, and preserve continuity when the operator changes.
stressors.residue: Model property owner, listing controller, licensed operator, co-host, service provider, guest contact, permit holder, payout beneficiary, fee recipient, and tax party as separate effective roles. Bookings and tasks resolve to the responsible role, while permissions, evidence, obligations, and financial splits remain independently revocable and auditable.

impacts.effect: Portfolio operations become a governed network of accountable owners, operators, and service partners.
Professional hosts can structure each property with explicit responsibilities and economics.
Assignment includes verified legal role, operational duty, permission, service level, and financial share.
Co-host adoption counts only active, verified, appropriately scoped operating relationships.
Adds role templates, qualification, task ownership, access review, and financial split management.
Routes each booking obligation to the accountable local role without sharing the owner's account.
Manages verified role, scope, duty, availability, service level, and revocation for each operating relationship.
Verifies people and organizations against the role they claim rather than one generic host identity.
Allocates fees, payouts, withholding, and tax evidence to the correct legal and economic parties.
Owns the professional role and obligation model with identity, payments, and policy teams.
Makes professional role governance and local accountability a supply-platform differentiator.

stressors.name: A city suspends all active stay permits and requires guests to relocate within twelve hours
stressors.detection: Emergency municipal order, permit-service updates, enforcement guidance, affected-address resolution, active-trip inventory, and guest or host confirmation.
stressors.attractor: A stay that was legal at check-in becomes prohibited while the guest is inside the property. The platform must stop the stay, find safe alternatives, protect evidence and money, and separate the guest's immediate need from later responsibility and appeal.
stressors.businessReaction: Identify every affected active stay, notify both parties, support safe departure and relocation, pause disputed payouts, preserve host appeal rights, and report complete remediation to the city.
stressors.residue: No new structural change is required: effective-dated eligibility identifies the precise stays whose permission changed, and the destination recovery model moves each guest commitment to a safe replacement, assistance, or refund path while preserving the original booking, evidence, and later financial decision.

impacts.effect: Guest trust includes a safe, accountable recovery when legal permission changes during an active stay.
The guest can recover through one trip path even though the trigger is legal rather than a property failure.
Reuses relocation, assistance, refund, and responsibility states already built for destination emergencies.
Resolution time measures complete guest relocation and host case establishment, not only permit deactivation.
Shows the mandatory departure, safe alternatives, support, and financial status in the existing trip recovery flow.
Combines an eligibility decision with the established area-level relocation process.
Applies the emergency order to active stays by address, permit, and effective time.
Coordinates relocation and later appeal through the existing recovery case.
Protects funds until emergency assistance, refund, host responsibility, and appeal are resolved.
Can execute the order through existing eligibility and recovery contracts rather than a new emergency system.
Makes compliant mid-stay relocation a concrete marketplace resilience benchmark.
